title: Work a chain of interlock bars in the only order it allows to reach a fuse carrier
instruction: Take the white fuse carrier out of the locked bay and set it on the green mat. The bay door is held by a chain of interlock bars. See how they block each other and slide them in order.
context: Switchgear technicians (O*NET 49-2095.00, Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Powerhouse, Substation, and Relay) meet panels whose door cannot open until bars are slid in one order, enforced by metal and not by a written procedure. They must see why a handle will not move and clear the cause. The board's 'Work out a two-lever combination lock and open the box' finds a combination by trying levers, 'Carry a trapped interlock key from a breaker to the matching door' carries a key, 'Run a full lockout cycle to change a machine's cutter' gives the steps and 'Open a drawer held shut by a bar' hides one blocker; here three bars and a door block each other in a visible chain, each bar moved locks the one before it, and the order has to be read from the hardware.
setup: Positions are cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); sizes are x by y by height. Table: oak top, with only the deck, the bay and the rail below on it. Deck: grey painted plywood box, 26 x 32.5 x 6 cm, x 12 to 38, y -20 to 12.5, fixed. Mat: green rubber sheet, 12 x 8.5 x 0.2 cm, on the deck's west end, centred at x 19, y 6.65 (x 13 to 25, y 2.4 to 10.9; 4 mm from bar B's handle and from the lug's path). Three painted hardwood bars, each 2 cm wide and 1.9 cm tall, ride 1 mm above the deck with light drag and no spring, and stay where they are left. Each bar is held by a 5 mm key under it running in a T-slot routed into the deck, so nothing stands proud of the deck where the tracks cross. Each has a 3 cm wide handle block, 5 cm tall, on top. Red bar A: x 15 to 17, y -19 to 1.5; handle x 14 to 18, y -16 to -13; slides along y, 4 cm toward -y. Yellow bar B: x 17.5 to 29.9, y -1 to 1; handle x 23 to 26, y -2 to 2; slides along x, 4 cm toward -x. Orange bar C: x 28 to 30, y 1.5 to 12.2; handle x 27 to 31, y 6 to 9; slides along y, 4 cm toward -y. Gaps at the start: A's side is 5 mm from B's -x end; B's side is 5 mm from C's tail; C's side is 5 mm from the door's lug. Bay: four dark grey plywood walls, 1 cm thick and 6 cm tall, fixed on the table around an opening x 24 to 37, y 13 to 24. The south wall (y 12 to 13, x 23 to 38) stands on the table and its foot overlaps the deck's north edge (y 12 to 12.5) by 5 mm, under the plate; the deck is notched there only along the lug's T-slot. Blue door: painted plywood plate, 14 x 12 x 1 cm, x 23.5 to 37.5, y 12.5 to 24.5, resting 1 mm above the walls as the bay's roof, with a 3.5 x 3.5 cm square window at x 28.75 to 32.25, y 16.75 to 20.25, through which the carrier's white top shows; handle block 3 x 4 x 4.9 cm at x 24.5 to 27.5, y 16 to 20; lug 2 x 1.2 x 2 cm at x 30.5 to 32.5, y 11.3 to 12.5; slides along x, 13 cm toward -x. The door is captured by a 5 mm key under the lug running in a T-slot routed into the deck (x 12 to 32.5, y 11.3 to 12.5, running the lug's whole path), and on the north side only by a brown hardwood rail, an inverted L 1 cm thick, x 10 to 38: its upright stands on the table, y 25 to 26, z 0 to 8.2 cm, and its lip reaches over the plate's north edge at y 24 to 25, z 7.2 to 8.2 cm, 1 mm above the plate; so the door can only slide. Fuse carrier: white plastic block, 4.5 x 4.5 x 5 cm, 60 g, on the table inside the bay, centred at x 30.5, y 18.5, 1 cm under the door.
scoring: Measured at the end, after opening the grippers, with a tape (how far a handle has moved from its start) and a top photo taken straight down (carrier against the mat). 0.2: bar A moved 2.4 cm or more. 0.4: and bar B 1.8 cm or more. 0.6: and bar C 0.8 cm or more. 0.8: and the door 10 cm or more. 1.0: bars A, B and C moved that far and the carrier wholly inside the mat, its bottom within 1 cm of the deck top, tilted at most 10 degrees (one bottom edge at most 8 mm higher than the opposite edge). Bands 0.2 to 0.8 each need the ones before it; 1.0 does not need the door to stay open once the carrier is out. A carrier still held more than 1 cm above the deck counts as not placed. A carrier dropped outside the mat or still in the bay earns no more than the band the bars and door reached. Otherwise 0.
reset_notes: Stand the carrier back in the bay, centred at x 30.5, y 18.5, with the door still open. Then slide the door, bar C, bar B and bar A back to their start stops, in that order, since each moved bar blocks the one before it.
fidelity: Approximate. Bars and door are boxes on slide joints with damping and no springs, held 1 mm off the deck; real interlocks use cams and pins. The carrier is a plain block. The simulator scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a carrier held more than 1 cm above the deck counts as not placed. The T-slots and keys under the bars and lug are for a real build and are not modelled; slide joints stand in for them.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (reached the right arm over the bay, bars, door and carrier stayed put); Dream-1 trials: 0 of 3 at full score (0, 0, 0); demo: 1.0 (slid the bars and door in order, then set the carrier on the green mat)
